chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds.
Except for what they voluntarily accept from his suggestions.

key_terms.الْأَوْسَاسُ: The depths or core of the soul/self (singular: وَسْواس)

ai.seo_question: What is the extent of Satan's authority over believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that Satan's dominion is restricted to *ausas* (his whispers or suggestions) which believers voluntarily accept, thereby emphasizing human agency in spiritual struggle. This conditional authority underscores the Shia theological principle that while Satan incites, he does not compel, making the believer's conscious choice the decisive factor in maintaining faith. The narration serves as a foundational proof for the concept of *ikhtiyar* (free will) against deterministic views of evil influence.
